summary: Full wizard UI test for RetailCLIQ Import Wizard. All 11 test items validated. Found and fixed 1 critical bug: stale doNext closure preventing Step1→Step2 navigation after GL account selection.

integration_issues.flow: Step1 → Step2 navigation via Continue button
integration_issues.issue: FIXED: Purchase Account (GL) selection via GlAccountSearch combobox did not persist in doNext handler due to stale closure. useEffect registering setNextHandler had deps [srcReady, creating, ws.file, ws.rows.length] but not doNext. After GL selection cfg.purchaseAccount changed, doNext was recreated, but setNextHandler wasn't re-called with the new handler. Fix: added doNextRef.current pattern so registered handler always calls latest doNext.

critical_code_review_comments: Bug fixed: Step1Source.jsx useEffect for setNextHandler now uses doNextRef.current pattern to avoid stale closure — the doNextRef is always updated to the latest doNext on every render, so the registered handler always has access to the current cfg.purchaseAccount value.
Note: ExpiryDate and TransDate columns detected as 'integer' (likely date columns stored as HBS/DMY) — no bug, by design

rca_of_issue: Root cause: In Step1Source.jsx, doNext is defined via useCallback([ws, cfg, patch, goNext]) so it recreates when cfg changes. But the useEffect calling setNextHandler(doNext) had deps [srcReady, creating, ws.file, ws.rows.length] — not including doNext. So when a user selected a GL account (updating cfg.purchaseAccount), doNext was recreated with the new cfg, but setNextHandler was NOT called again. WizardContext's nextHandlerRef.current still pointed to the old doNext (with empty purchaseAccount). Fix: replaced setNextHandler(doNext) with setNextHandler(() => doNextRef.current()), where doNextRef.current = doNext is updated on every render. This breaks the closure dependency without causing infinite loops.
